mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months raises discount rates, reducing present value of future corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns, provided the economy is not in recession.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE not below 4% in last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes despite rising rates.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months when UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the previous year's level for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative equity returns over the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous year for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) indicates more workers entering the market without corresponding job growth, which can depress wage growth and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable (±0.1pp) while PAYEMS rises >0.3% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes under these labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising while PAYEMS grows slowly) signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces demand for goods and services and is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS grows >2% YoY while PAYEMS grows <1% YoY for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).
